findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client upgrades Forge, then starts a user-facing story from a signed prototype containing the copied renderer.
Sync rewrites the renderer inside the approved design folder, changing its Git tree ID. The signed decision still contains the old ID: `src/forge/design.py:35-38` copies it into new plans, and `src/forge/design.py:117-122` rejects it when `forge read` checks the folder. Existing approved stories can similarly fail task start or close after taking the upgrade. The ruling to refresh header-marked copies did not account for these approval hashes.
Adds work: keep design approvals valid when refreshing renderers; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Refreshing renderers invalidates approved design trees

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client with five saved, header-marked renderers upgrades Forge without custom generated-file attributes.
The upgrade rewrites those five files, but the generated-output check reconstructs sync inputs without `docs/design` (`src/forge/sync.py:474-478` and `src/forge/sync.py:502-525`). The pre-commit hook therefore counts the renderers plus `forge.toml` as six code files and refuses the upgrade commit under the five-file limit (`src/forge/githooks.py:230-241`). The upgrade path stages these changes together at `src/forge/upgrade.py:177-190`, so it cannot reach close.
Adds work: recognize refreshed renderers in the existing sync-output check; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
